role_note: The strongest honest LLM-only baseline on ToN-IoT: a per-fold MLP head trained on the same CySecBERT KG embeddings, with AGAF head fusion. This is NOT a rung of the canonical ladder. The canonical architecture uses the whitened-prototype consultant on every rung, matching UNSW-NB15 — see results/ton_iot_current.json.

source_artifacts.command: python -m src.pipeline.step3.train_fusion --dataset ton_iot --use-head-logits --output-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step3_fusion_head && python -m src.pipeline.step4.train_feedback --dataset ton_iot --use-llm-head --top-k-percent 15.0 --agaf-benchmark-path data/ton_iot/processed/step3_fusion_head/benchmark_summary.json --output-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step4_feedback_head15 && python -m src.pipeline.step4.assemble_ladder --dataset ton_iot --use-llm-head --fusion-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step3_fusion_head --feedback-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step4_feedback_head15

must_be_reported: Under the head consultant the ToN ladder does not hold and nothing at the top is significantly ordered: AGAF ties the LLM (-0.0025, CI [-0.0110, +0.0023]), the loop ties AGAF (-0.0149, CI [-0.0462, +0.0160]), the loop ties the LLM (-0.0173, CI [-0.0476, +0.0123]). Only the GNN is clearly separated at the bottom.
The trained LLM head alone scores 0.5165, above every other rung including the loop (0.4986). As on UNSW, an MLP on the KG embeddings matches or beats the full system.

AGAF's learned output gate stayed at its 0.95 initialisation (trained bias 2.9947 vs init 3.0), so AGAF defers ~95% to the head and reproduces it almost class for class. Disabling the gate-entropy regulariser produced bit-identical predictions, so the entropy term is not the cause.
